key_insight: BeatGraph shifts ECG representation from fixed-length patches to heartbeat-aware structure, which is a better fit for infant ECGs. This helps foundation models preserve cardiac events that patching can split or distort.
problem_solved: Most ECG foundation models use arbitrary patches that can cut across heartbeats and vary in beat count as heart rate changes. This is especially problematic for infants, whose ECG signals and heart rates differ substantially from adult clinic data.
method: Represent ECG as graphs built around individual heartbeats instead of fixed-length time patches.
Use self-supervised learning to learn heartbeat-level representations from home-recorded infant ECGs.
Design the representation to better capture infant-specific cardiac structure and variable heart rate.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights the importance of signal structure-aware tokenization when adapting foundation models to medical data. It suggests a more robust path for learning infant ECG representations in realistic home environments.
